Morning team —

Per our plan to run a short weekly sync on dedicated capacity sizing, I wanted to surface the most immediate asks from the field and get alignment on how we provision for the next 90 days. Quick context: two deals we expect to close within Q3 will materially affect our H100 pool needs if they convert at full committed throughput. I'm attaching a working forecast (Q2-fleet-forecast.xlsx) with deal-level scenarios.

Top-line asks:
- Priyom: confirm likelihood (P-win %) and expected start date for the two priority deals listed (D-2026-1473, D-2026-1519). Include any contract language that requires dedicated reserved capacity.
- Logan: what is realistic lead time to add H100 cards to Dedicated (on-prem vs cloud burst), and what short-term mitigations can we run (quantization, prefix caching, reduced concurrency)?
- Laura: what price/commit thresholds do we need to hit to justify reserving an extra pod? Also confirm billing/timing constraints for committed capacity orders.

Immediate numbers from pipeline (see sheet, high-level):
- D-2026-1473 (VectorAI) — requested 12 x H100-equivalent GPUs capacity at 8k tokens/min sustained, targeted start ~2026-08-01, P-win 65% (sales notes).
- D-2026-1519 (Acme Payments) — pilot to production ramp to 6 x H100-equivalent GPUs, targeted start ~2026-07-15 if contract signed, P-win 55%.
- Other smaller requests (total ~4 H100-equivalent) scattered Q3.

Risk profile: if both convert at full throughput, we need +22 H100-equivalent capacity by mid-August. We have ~10 H100-equivalent free in Dedicated today when accounting for buffer; acquisitions/provisioning needed for the remainder.

Please reply inline with one-line commitments where possible. I'll pull this into the weekly snapshot and propose a procurement plan by Wednesday.

Thanks —
Sean

Sean / team —

Appreciate the heads-up. A few infrastructure realities and options:

1) Lead times and procurement
- H100 discrete cards (on-prem) have ~8–12 week lead time today for new hardware; ordering this week could deliver mid-August at earliest.
- If we want guaranteed capacity before mid-August, we should either: a) pre-book cloud-burst capacity with a hyperscaler marketplace partner (fast but expensive), or b) negotiate a short-term rental from our hardware partner for ~6–10 weeks (mid cost).

2) Software mitigations (short-term, low cost)
- Aggressive quantization to 4-bit for non-sensitive workloads — expect ~1.6x throughput improvement, but needs evaluation on VectorAI models (quality risk).
- Increase batch windows for non-latency-critical routes — saves ~20–30% token cost at cost of latency increase for some requests.
- KV prefix caching for repeat prompts (VectorAI and Acme have a fair amount of repeated context) — could shave ~15% effective capacity needs.

3) Dedicated pod sizing and mapping
- If both deals hit full committed throughput, recommendation is: reserve 16 H100-equivalent to be safe (we currently can free up ~10 by moving low-priority workloads to shared host or reducing concurrency). We should avoid overcommit beyond that until P-win > 80%.

4) Costs and procurement process
- Lead time + procurement approvals will need a signed statement of work (SOW) to trigger hardware purchase. If finance needs assurances, we can do a 3-month rental to bridge to purchase.

Action items I need:
- Priyom: firm earliest start dates and whether customers will accept phased delivery or short-term cloud burst.
- Laura: confirm finance appetite for a rental-to-purchase bridge (cost delta and accounting treatment).

I'll run a quick simulation tomorrow with two scenarios (cloud-burst vs rental bridge) and share numbers.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Weekly fleet planning: aligning dedicated capacity with pipeline (June 14)

Thanks, all. Quick finance perspective:

- Commitment economics
  - For a 12-month reserved commitment, unit cost for H100-equivalent drops ~35% vs. on-demand cloud burst. For a 3–6 month rental, we're roughly 10–15% cheaper than cloud on-demand but ~15–25% more expensive than a 12-month commit.
  - Given sales P-win today, reserving a full pod (16 H100-equivalent) now would be a stretch on our cash runway unless we have signed SOWs covering >60% of the capacity within 45 days.

- Recommended path
  1) Approve a 6–8 week rental bridge to handle the likely July–August ramp (low capex, quicker). Cost center to be Product Ops with a contingency cap of $450k — requires VP approval.
  2) If both deals sign by end of July, convert rental to a 12-month reserved purchase with backdated credit where possible.

- Accounting/timing note: rental payments will hit OpEx; purchase would be CapEx. Need procurement and legal to prepare a convertible SOW that allows crediting rental payments against a purchase if conversion happens.

I've uploaded a short memo with numbers: commit-vs-on-demand.pdf. Happy to run the exact impact to Q3 forecast in today's finance call if helpful.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
VP Finance, Redwood Inference
